twitter_thread: Most QA teams are paying $36/user/month for test management tools built for a different era. Here's what modern QA teams actually need — and why legacy tools consistently fall short. 🧵

Problem 1: Rigidity. TestRail's folder structure works for stable test suites. It breaks for agile teams where organization needs to shift every sprint. Reorganizing mid-cycle is a multi-hour project. It should take minutes.

Problem 2: Price. TestRail at $36/user/month = $4,320/year for a 10-person team. Before Jira, CI/CD, or anything else. The pricing was designed for enterprise procurement, not for QA leads with a credit card.
Problem 3: Jira dependency. Zephyr and Xray require Jira seats for everyone who needs visibility. Your PM wants to see test coverage? Jira seat. Developer wants to check failing tests? Jira seat.

What modern QA teams actually need: flexible structure (tags + folders), real collaboration (shareable dashboards, no account required), fair pricing ($10/user/month), fast migration, context-aware AI, and performance at scale.
